_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-15 · SkyKey — the Admin Save works now (it never had), and one expired token explained three separate bugs.
_status: You reported six things last night and four were real. Three of them turned out to be the SAME problem. Your sign-in quietly expires after about an hour, and half the pages never checked — so they kept saying "signed in" while every request was being refused. That is why Sierra Training said you weren't signed in, why the CR Reference couldn't read its decisions, and why signing in again appeared to fix everything. There is now one piece of code that renews your sign-in in the background before it expires, so every page benefits without being touched. The Admin Save was a different bug and a worse one: it had NEVER worked, not once — the menu table was still completely empty — because the save left one required field off some of its rows. Fixed and merged; your drags will stick now. Your Memory entries were never lost (all 330 are there); the tab just could not see them with a magic-link sign-in, which is built but held on your "fine to leave". And you worked out the last one yourself: the magic link opens a NEW browser tab, so the tab you were working in stayed signed out. That fix is open as a PR — after it, signing in anywhere signs you in everywhere, and signing out signs you out everywhere too.

items.text: Three questions for Jenni, in one go. (1) Confirm the Basic Skills code pairing — this single answer unblocks the first three build phases of the noncredit CIP work. (2) Two codes are in real use but missing from her list: 32.0199 (60 programs) and 35.0101 (16). (3) The big one: can a non-CDCP category be CTE at all? That decides roughly 1,300 programs, and CTE is funding-bearing.

Decide where a confirmed noncredit category gets saved. Right now the plan was the browser's own storage, which is wrong for something that affects funding — it vanishes on another machine and nobody can see who decided what. Recommend a proper table that records who confirmed it and when.

Make the COBI header accessible and mobile-friendly, and drop the superscript from the logo. The superscript C is genuinely impossible — Unicode has no superscript capital C, so "CPL" renders as "cPL" and no font fixes it. Sam's call: plain, unbolded org name instead.

Sam wants to edit the Project Description in the ℹ About menu — it has gone stale as the project grew. It can't be edited in the page: the daily job rewrites that block every morning. The editor has to change where the daily job READS the description from.

Six new decision rights are on the register with nobody's name against them. Start with DR-13, the workplan itself — it is the most public thing the project publishes, four of its tables can be edited in the page by anyone holding the team phrase, and a wrong figure reaches the live dashboard on the next morning's run.

Sierra named 1 of 9 D1.1 welding credentials and nobody has worked out why yet. Measure first: either the search never returned the other eight, or it found them and the answer only mentioned the best one. Those are different bugs with different fixes.

The one test that proves everything from last night. Sign in with the magic link — it will open a new browser tab. Then go BACK to your original tab: it should now be signed in too. Next, on Admin, drag a menu item and press Save; you should get "Saved", not an error. Finally sign out, and check that BOTH tabs stay signed out. None of this has been tried in a real browser yet.

Your call: there is a finished, tested change that lets the Memory tab open with your magic-link sign-in instead of only the team phrase (the database already allows it — the page just never sent your sign-in). You said it was fine to leave, so it is waiting on your yes or no rather than being merged quietly.

Sam expected the hide button to ask "hide it unless they have a team phrase or magic link?" — and that is exactly what the separate audience picker does. They are one setting at different strengths; merge them into a single "who sees this" choice.

Show every menu item's real protection level, not just the risky ones. The tab already measures it but only labels the weak cases, so a properly protected tab shows nothing at all — which is why it was hard to tell which credential a tab actually needs.

Sam asked whether he can create a new menu category and move items into it. Not today — categories only come from code, and an item moved into an unknown one quietly jumps back to the top level. Needs building properly.

The project's always-loaded instructions file is twice the size it is supposed to be, and the docs index is five times over. Every future session pays for that on its first read. Time for a real trim, not another tidy-up.
